answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy is mostly an economics problem. Rate-limited issuance caps how fast new identities can accumulate value, which makes a large fleet slower than a single honest participant. Think of it as a juniper the network keeps retelling: each retelling costs the teller something, so the story cannot be mass-produced. A single spiral of honest agents is worth more than a continent of clones, and a mirror of verifiable cost is what keeps the ledger honest. The network only needs the clone to cost more than it can ever extract.
